metadata.title: Convex Modeling of Price Cross-Impact over Time

finalAnalysis.summary: 関連先物間のcross-impactと時系列上のtransient impactを同時に表す、凸二次の取引コストモデルを提案する。各期の正半定値impact matrixをpower-law decay kernelで結合し、流動性が時間変動しても価格操作を許さない構成を示す。WTIカレンダースプレッドの事例では、分離型コストモデルより相対価値取引のimpactを低く評価し、より積極的なポジションを生成したと報告している。
finalAnalysis.mainResult: power-law kernelから構成した時間行列$G$が正半定値であるため、全期間のコスト行列$A=B(G\otimes I_n)B$も$A\succeq 0$となり、任意の取引列$u$について$u^\top A u\geq 0$が成立する。したがって、モデル上は負コストのround tripが排除される。2004～2011年のWTI事例では、月平均net P&Lがgross limit比で提案モデル3.1 bp、self-impactモデル2.3 bp、分離型baseline 0.4 bpだったと報告されている。
finalAnalysis.practicalApplication: 商品・金利・マクロ市場のcalendar spreadやcurve tradeについて、相関するlegsのimpact相殺、entryからexitまで残るimpact、予定された流動性変化を含めて、複数日の建玉と解消を凸最適化できる。特にindex roll、満期、指標発表、settlement windowのように流動性が予測可能な局面に適する。
finalAnalysis.methodology: 各期のself-impactを予測volatilityとvolumeから設定し、return correlationをimpact correlationのproxyとして正半定値行列$\Lambda_t$を構成する。時間方向には$k(h)=(1+h/\tau)^{-\beta}$を用い、対称結合$\Lambda_t^{1/2}\Lambda_s^{1/2}$によって凸性を保証する。実証ではWTI期近・期先の2限月を対象に、期待収益、impact、bid/ask spread、CVaR制約を含むmulti-period optimizationを月初に解き、3種類のコスト仕様を比較した。
finalAnalysis.limitations: 単一銘柄impactを線形とし、実証的に知られるsquare-root lawを再現していない。取引所の限月別volumeを利用できないためvolume推移をシミュレーションし、impact scaleも推定せず$\ell_i=1$と置いている。return correlationをcross-impactのproxyとし、日次settlement dataだけを使うため、order bookや実約定に基づく検証ではない。さらに提案モデル自身をsimulated impact costの評価器にも用いており比較に循環性があるほか、単一市場・2004～2011年の96か月に限定され、統計的不確実性やout-of-sample性能は十分に示されていない。対称結合はno-manipulationを保証する設計上の近似であり、真の因果的impact dynamicsを推定したものではない。
finalAnalysis.reason: cross-impact、transient impact、時間変動する流動性を一つの計算可能な凸モデルに統合し、no-price-manipulationを数学的に保証する点は、multi-asset executionとrelative-value portfolio constructionに直接有用である。一方、実証はシミュレーション依存で、提案モデルを評価器にも使っているため、報告されたP&L改善を実運用上の優位性と解釈するには追加検証が必要である。

english.summary: The paper proposes a convex quadratic transaction-cost model that jointly represents cross-impact among related futures and transient impact over time. It couples positive semidefinite period-level impact matrices through a power-law decay kernel and shows that the construction excludes price manipulation even when liquidity varies over time. In a WTI calendar-spread study, the authors report that it assigns lower impact to relative-value trades and produces larger positions than separable cost models.
english.mainResult: Because the temporal matrix $G$ generated by the power-law kernel is positive semidefinite, the full-horizon cost matrix $A=B(G\otimes I_n)B$ also satisfies $A\succeq 0$, implying $u^\top A u\geq 0$ for every trade sequence $u$. The model therefore excludes negative-cost round trips. In the 2004–2011 WTI study, the reported average monthly net P&L as a fraction of the gross limit is 3.1 bp for the proposed model, 2.3 bp for the self-impact model, and 0.4 bp for the separable baseline.
english.practicalApplication: The framework supports convex optimization of multi-day entry and exit schedules for calendar spreads and curve trades in commodity, rates, and macro markets, accounting for impact netting across correlated legs, residual impact between entry and exit, and scheduled liquidity changes. It is particularly relevant around index rolls, expiries, economic announcements, and settlement windows.
english.methodology: The authors set period-level self-impact from forecast volatility and volume, use return correlation as a proxy for impact correlation, and construct a positive semidefinite matrix $\Lambda_t$. They use the temporal kernel $k(h)=(1+h/\tau)^{-\beta}$ and guarantee convexity through the symmetric coupling $\Lambda_t^{1/2}\Lambda_s^{1/2}$. The empirical study applies multi-period optimization with expected return, impact, bid/ask spread, and CVaR constraints to nearby and deferred WTI contracts, solving once before each month and comparing three cost specifications.
english.limitations: Single-asset impact is linear and does not reproduce the empirically documented square-root law. Contract-level exchange volume is unavailable, so the volume path is simulated, while the impact scale is not estimated and is fixed at $\ell_i=1$. Return correlation is used as a proxy for cross-impact, and the analysis relies on daily settlement data rather than order-book or execution data. The proposed model is also used to calculate simulated impact costs, creating circularity in the comparison; the study is limited to one market and 96 months from 2004–2011, with limited evidence on statistical uncertainty or out-of-sample performance. The symmetric coupling is a design approximation that guarantees no manipulation rather than an estimate of the true causal impact dynamics.
english.reason: The integration of cross-impact, transient impact, and time-varying liquidity into one tractable convex model, together with a mathematical no-price-manipulation guarantee, is directly useful for multi-asset execution and relative-value portfolio construction. However, the empirical analysis depends heavily on simulation and uses the proposed model as an evaluator, so further validation is required before treating the reported P&L improvement as evidence of live-trading superiority.

metadata.title: Artificial Intelligence in Equity and Crypto Markets: Progress, Profitability Evidence, and the Limits of Automated Investing

finalAnalysis.summary: 株式・ETF・中央集権型crypto spot、perpetual futures、DEXを対象に、ML、time-series foundation model、金融LLM、RL、agentの投資利用を批判的に整理したレビューである。予測やテキスト処理、portfolio設計、workflow統合では進歩が報告される一方、取引費用、capacity、時点整合性、リスク調整を満たす持続的なnet alphaの公開証拠は乏しいと結論づける。
finalAnalysis.mainResult: 著者らが調査した公開研究の範囲では、特定のAI architectureがregime横断的かつcapacity-awareな持続的net alphaを一般に生むとは確認できない。好成績のhistorical backtestは存在するが、look-ahead bias、LLMのmemorization、multiple testing、signal decay、market impact、funding、liquidation、gas、MEVなどにより、予測性能から実現収益への変換が崩れ得ると報告する。
finalAnalysis.practicalApplication: 実務では、データとmodel checkpointのpoint-in-time管理、signal・portfolio・executionの共同評価、規模別capacity curve、実行可能価格によるcost modeling、事前確定したforward testを導入すべきである。株式、spot、perpetual、DEXでP&Lと執行リスクを分離し、注文権限を持つagentには銘柄・notional・leverage制限、price collar、reconciliation、外部kill switchを設ける必要がある。
finalAnalysis.methodology: 2026年8月31日までの研究と一次的な公式資料を対象にしたcritical state-of-the-art reviewであり、systematic reviewやmeta-analysisではない。証拠を、temporality、selection control、portfolio mapping、implementation realism、risk/benchmark、external validity、operational provenanceの7次元で評価し、point-in-time情報からsignal、position、order/fill、費用控除後収益、持続性へ至るalpha-translation chainで比較する。
finalAnalysis.limitations: 網羅的なdatabase検索、重複した独立screening、事前登録protocol、全研究へのformal risk-of-bias scoring、定量的なeffect poolingは行っていない。対象研究の市場、期間、benchmark、cost modelが不均一で、cryptoとaudited live-capitalの証拠は特に薄い。公式product資料は機能の存在しか示さず、引用されたpreprintや著者実施benchmarkも独立検証ではないため、本稿の結論は公開情報に限定される。
finalAnalysis.reason: 電子執行とmarket microstructureの観点から、AIの予測精度を収益性と同一視せず、spread、impact、latency、borrow、funding、liquidation、gas、MEV、capacityまで監査する統一的な枠組みが有用である。新規の実証推定や特定戦略の性能証明ではないが、AI trading研究を評価・設計するための実務的なチェックリストとして推奨できる。金利モデルやyield curveへの直接的な貢献はない。

english.summary: This critical review covers the use of ML, time-series foundation models, financial LLMs, RL, and agents across equities, ETFs, centralized crypto spot, perpetual futures, and DEXs. It reports progress in prediction, text processing, portfolio design, and workflow integration, but concludes that public evidence for persistent net alpha after costs, capacity constraints, temporal validation, and risk adjustment remains limited.
english.mainResult: Within the public research examined by the authors, no particular AI architecture is shown to generate persistent, cross-regime, capacity-aware net alpha in general. Although strong historical backtests exist, the paper reports that translation from predictive performance to realized returns can fail because of look-ahead bias, LLM memorization, multiple testing, signal decay, market impact, funding, liquidation, gas, and MEV.
english.practicalApplication: Practitioners should use point-in-time data and model checkpoints, jointly evaluate signals, portfolios, and execution, report capacity curves by scale, model costs using executable prices, and conduct precommitted forward tests. P&L and execution risks should be separated across equities, spot, perpetuals, and DEXs, while order-capable agents require instrument, notional, and leverage limits, price collars, reconciliation, and an external kill switch.
english.methodology: The paper is a critical state-of-the-art review of research and primary official material available through 31 August 2026, rather than a systematic review or meta-analysis. It evaluates evidence across seven dimensions—temporality, selection control, portfolio mapping, implementation realism, risk and benchmark specification, external validity, and operational provenance—and compares studies through an alpha-translation chain from point-in-time information to signals, positions, orders and fills, net returns, and persistence.
english.limitations: The review does not provide an exhaustive database search, duplicate independent screening, a preregistered protocol, formal risk-of-bias scores for every study, or quantitative effect pooling. The underlying studies use heterogeneous markets, periods, benchmarks, and cost models, while evidence for crypto and audited live-capital performance is especially sparse. Official product materials establish only capability, and cited preprints or author-run benchmarks are not independent validation, so the conclusions are limited to the public record.
english.reason: The paper provides a useful framework for electronic execution and market-microstructure analysis by refusing to equate AI predictive accuracy with profitability and by auditing spreads, impact, latency, borrow, funding, liquidation, gas, MEV, and capacity. It does not offer new empirical estimates or prove the performance of a specific strategy, but it is recommended as a practical checklist for evaluating and designing AI trading research. It makes no direct contribution to interest-rate models or yield curves.
